thread:
customer_jane: Hey @support, since the cert rotation at ~19:02 UTC a subset of our API calls to hosted.redwood.ai are failing with 502/gateway and client TLS handshake timeout. Happening from multiple regions. Attaching a small client log excerpt:

customer_jane: ```
2026-11-05T19:04:12Z ERR api request failed: handshake timeout after 10s, remote_addr=34.120.45.99:443
2026-11-05T19:04:13Z ERR retrying...
2026-11-05T19:04:13Z ERR final: 502 Bad Gateway
```

customer_jane: We can reproduce with a simple curl from our prod VPC: `curl -v https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate` shows TLS handshake stalls then aborts. Any idea? This started immediately after your cert rotation message.

support_alan: Thanks @customer_jane — sorry for the interruption. Can you paste the full `curl -v` output (no secrets) and the public IP you're calling from? Also confirming: you saw our deploy-bot cert rotation earlier?

deploy-bot: cert-rotate job `cert-rotate-prod-2026-11-05-18-58` completed successfully at 2026-11-05T18:58:40Z (image: cert-rotation-service v2.4.1) :white_check_mark:

customer_jane: here's the curl output (sanitized):

customer_jane: ```
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate
*   Trying 34.120.45.99...
* Connected to api.hosted.redwood.ai (34.120.45.99) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (IN), Cipher is (NONE)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
* TLS handshake timeout
* Failed to connect to api.hosted.redwood.ai port 443: TLS handshake timeout
```

support_alan: Good repro, thanks. @eng_maya / @networking_tom can you look at edge certificates + DNS for the IP above?

eng_maya: Looking. First quick check: openssl s_client against 34.120.45.99 from our office shows an incomplete chain: `error:14090086:SSL routines:ssl3_get_server_certificate:certificate verify failed` and `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`. Might be missing intermediate. Pasting sanitized openssl output: ```
CONNECTED(00000005)
depth=0 CN = api.hosted.redwood.ai
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN = api.hosted.redwood.ai
   i:CN = Redwood Prod Issuer
---
```

networking_tom: Running `dig +trace api.hosted.redwood.ai` shows the authoritative records changed but some recursive resolvers still returning the old A record (34.120.45.99) which points to the old edge pool that expects the previous cert chain. Looks like TTLs were high and CDNs/ISPs haven't cleared yet.

networking_tom: Snapshots: `authoritative A -> 34.122.100.11` (new pool) but `some resolvers -> 34.120.45.99` (old pool). TTL was 3600 before rotation.

oncall_sre_lee: If clients hit old pool that doesn't have the fullchain deployed yet, they'll see handshake failures. Two-prong: invalid cert chain OR SNI mismatch. Any sign of SNI config drift?

eng_maya: We checked SNI, config present. Root cause appears to be the cert rotation job deployed the new leaf cert to new pool but failed to upload the intermediate to the old warm pool due to a race in the rollout script. Deploy-bot shows success for the main job but one sidecar upload timed out. We're investigating logs.

cdn_ops: CDN edge caches also have long-lived DNS caches in some edge POPs. Purging will help for clients that go through the CDN.

support_alan: Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) rollback cert on impacted old pool OR 2) push fullchain to old pool, 3) purge CDN caches, 4) request customer to flush local resolver cache or retry. Which is fastest?

eng_maya: Quickest is to push the missing intermediate to the old pool and restart TLS sidecar on those hosts. Doing that now. I'll also trigger a CDN purge and reduce authoritative TTL to 60s to accelerate convergence.

security_zoe: Note: pushing fullchain is safe; ensure private key stays on intended hosts only. We'll watch audit logs.

eng_maya: Pushed fullchain.pem to warm pool hosts, restarted sidecar: `systemctl restart redwood-edge-tls` (restart logs show successful handshake bindings).

networking_tom: Purged CDN caches and lowered TTL to 60. Also triggered `ndots` advisory to ops teams to nudge partners. Running `dig` from multiple public resolvers now shows new A record propagating.

support_alan: @customer_jane can you try your curl again? Also if you can try from two clients/regions that'd help confirm.

customer_jane: Re-tested from our prod VPC and eu-west client: both successful now. Curl output:```
* Connected to api.hosted.redwood.ai (34.122.100.11) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (IN), Cipher is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

customer_jane: Thanks, looks resolved. Appreciate the fast response :thumbsup:

support_alan: Great — marking as resolved for now. We'll keep thread open until tomorrow to watch metrics.

eng_maya: Postmortem notes to add: 1) cert rotation job needs stronger verification: verify fullchain presence on all active and warm pools before switch, 2) lower pre-rotation TTL for critical hostnames, 3) add a rollout step that purges key CDN caches as part of rotation, 4) add alert for `verify error:num=20` spikes in edge logs.

oncall_sre_lee: Also adding an automation to retry sidecar uploads with exponential backoff; current one-time upload caused the gap.

customer_jane: We'll keep an eye on it but good to close from our side. Thanks everyone.

support_alan: Logged follow-ups in internal ticket INF-7123, assigned to eng_maya and networking_tom. Closing thread in 24h if no regression.

deploy-bot: Rollback not required; update to prod cert rollout recorded in release history `cert-rotate-prod-2026-11-05-18-58` -> note: intermediate fix applied to warm pool at 2026-11-05T19:07:22Z.
